title: Syria denies sending troops to fight Houthis in return for Saudi loans
author: Amberin Zaman
text:
Analysis

Syria denies sending troops to fight Houthis in return for Saudi loans

The Saudi Fund for Development and Syria’s Finance Ministry recently inked more than $403 million in concessional loan agreements, fueling speculation that Damascus agreed to provide military support to Saudi Arabia in exchange for financial aid.

Amberin Zaman

Nov 9, 2026

Add AL-MONITOR on Google

Saudi Arabia's Deputy Foreign Minister Waleed el-Khereiji (R) speaks with Syria's interim Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shibani during a meeting of the Council of Arab Foreign Ministers at the Arab League headquarters in central Cairo on Sept. 7, 2026. — Khaled Desouki / AFP via Getty Images

Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shibani refuted reports on Monday that Syrian forces had been deployed to Yemen to help Saudi Arabia fight Iran-backed Houthis.Speaking at a joint news conference with his Jordanian counterpart, Ayman Safadi, at Damascus’ Tishreen Palace, Shibani said, “There is no deployment of forces in Yemen and there is not even a plan in the near future for that. We today have an agreement with Saudi Arabia, and any military plan outside of the borders will be announced and will be spoken of and won’t be hidden.”Shibani continued, “Our military agreement with Saudi Arabia focuses on rebuilding Syria’s armed forces.”The rebuttal follows news reports over the past three days about the alleged deployment of Syrian troops to the kingdom and to Yemen.
